3 ways leaders could avert an AI doomsday scenario

As scientists warn about the risk of AI killing us all, the question is why governments and companies haven't done more to reduce the risk.
The big picture: The same capabilities making AI economically valuable and increasingly useful also make advanced systems harder to contain.
Driving the news: Anthropic researchers warned Tuesday that rogue versions of superintelligent AI could destroy humanity, placing the odds in the double-digits.
Context: Researchers have been raising fears of AI doom for years, using the shorthand "p(doom)" to describe the probability of an AI-driven catastrophe.

Slow AI growth

AI developers have long called for slowdowns and pauses to ensure safeguards keep pace with increasingly powerful systems.
Flashback: In July, OpenAI and Anthropic supported a call on governments to establish a coordinated framework to slow down risky capability jumps.

Anthropic insiders warn AI could kill all humans

Three Anthropic researchers went public last night with chilling concerns about out-of-control AI, warning it could destroy humans this decade.
Why it matters: They're hardly alone. Their warnings came just days after top OpenAI leaders, including CEO Sam Altman, said AI is speeding into a scary, uncontrollable phase.
Warnings from inside the AI giants point to an epic shared dilemma: Slow down and risk falling behind, or press ahead and risk losing control. The companies are full speed ahead, even as they practically beg for regulation or a global pause, Axios' Maria Curi, Madison Mills and Ina Fried report.
The big picture: Calling this unprecedented would be a gross understatement. You basically have the fastest-growing companies in human history warning their products could harm or even destroy humanity.
🏛️ Context for readers from Mike & Jim: This is self-evidently scary stuff - and these vague warnings are impossible to validate or appraise. But we think readers, especially members of Congress and those in relevant federal agencies, need to be aware that the AI creators themselves see potential catastrophic outcomes absent a shift in how America, China and others review and release more powerful AI models.
💡 How to think about this: Nobody is warning AI is an imminent high-level threat. What they're saying is that the technology keeps improving faster than they thought possible and will soon be able to self-improve (recursive self-improvement). Once that happens, it gets even better, faster ... and much harder to predict or control.
